summary: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral (CGRS D) is a Government of Canada award run jointly by the three research agencies (CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC) for doctoral students in health, natural sciences and engineering, and social sciences and humanities. It gives CAD 40,000 a year for 36 months. International students can apply only if they are already registered in a doctoral programme at an eligible Canadian institution by the deadline, and up to 15% of awards are open to them. It is not a way to enter Canada.
eligibility_notes:
Study stage: you may have completed no more than 36 months of full-time-equivalent doctoral study by 31 December of the application year. Full-time months, including summers, count; two part-time terms count as one full-time term; study towards the same doctorate counts wherever it was done. Fast-track, joint and joint professional-PhD programmes have their own counting rules. The doctorate must be mainly research-based with a merit-reviewed thesis, project or equivalent.

International applicants: non-citizens, non-permanent residents and non-protected persons must be registered in an eligible Canadian doctoral programme by the application deadline; CIHR states that anyone not registered in a doctoral programme at a Canadian institution is ineligible. An approved leave of absence counts as registered. The page says up to 15% of awards are available to international applicants.

Holding the award outside Canada: only Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons (as of the deadline) who have completed at least one earlier undergraduate or graduate degree at a Canadian institution; up to 20% of doctoral awards may be held outside Canada.

Restrictions: only one Canada Research Training Awards Suite program per year across CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC; at most three applications to CGRS D; you cannot already hold a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC (including Vanier); CIHR and NSERC holders cannot hold a tenure or tenure-track appointment at the same time; you may not receive federal pay for the same studies. Applications can be written in English or French.

Choose the agency closest to your research subject; you are responsible for that choice and for sending the application through the correct channel (through your institution if it has a quota with that agency, otherwise directly to the agency). A wrong channel means rejection.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work experience requirement stated. The only time limit is no more than 36 months of full-time-equivalent doctoral study by 31 December of the application year.
funding_summary: CAD 40,000 per year for 36 months. The award may be held part-time with approval (value and duration may be prorated). Indigenous applicants applying through NSERC or SSHRC may receive a CAD 5,000 supplement for one year, and some extra awards go to applications that match priority research areas. Paid parental leave of up to 12 months and other interruptions can extend the end date.
programmes_note: Doctoral research in health (CIHR), natural sciences and engineering (NSERC), and social sciences and humanities (SSHRC), including interdisciplinary work; the agency whose subject area is closest to your research is the one you apply to. Some additional awards may go to strong applications in priority research areas: advanced digital technologies (AI, quantum, cybersecurity); health, including biotechnology; clean technology and resource value chains; environment, climate resilience and the Arctic; food and water security; democratic and community resilience; manufacturing and advanced materials; defence and dual-use technologies.
institutions_note: Eligible Canadian institutions. Each agency gives every institution a quota, which is the maximum number of applications it may forward, and the institution reviews on merit and sets its own earlier internal deadline. If your institution has no quota with the agency you choose, you apply directly to that agency. Where you apply from does not decide where you hold the award.

summary.detail: Doctoral study at an eligible Canadian institution, up to 36 months of full-time-equivalent study completed by 31 December of the application year; CAD 40,000 a year for 36 months; research-oriented programmes only. International students must already be registered in the doctorate.

benefits.conditions: Paid to the award holder; a Canadian institution pays on its own schedule, and awards held abroad are paid directly by the agency (NSERC and SSHRC twice a year, CIHR quarterly). Part-time holding is allowed with approval and may prorate value and duration. Amounts paid for periods when you were no longer eligible must be repaid.

benefits.limit_text: CAD 5,000 supplement for one year for Indigenous applicants (First Nations, Inuit, Metis) applying through NSERC or SSHRC
benefits.conditions: Under the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative; CIHR has its own funding route for Indigenous applicants.

benefits.limit_text: Extra awards for applications matching priority research areas, and up to 10 extra awards per agency reserved for self-identified Black applicants who consent to be considered
benefits.conditions: Applicants stay in the open competition first. Selected at the agency's discretion.

requirements.text: Online application in the agency's system: ResearchNet for CIHR (with a CIHR PIN), the NSERC online system with Form 201 for NSERC, and the SSHRC online form for SSHRC. Equity, diversity and inclusion self-identification forms are completed before the deadline at CIHR; the SSHRC form includes a mandatory diversity considerations module of up to 1,700 characters.

Common CV: validated CIHR Academic CV (CIHR) or verified SSHRC web CV (SSHRC). Only applicants, not supervisors, submit a CV. List all degrees, awards, employment, activities and contributions; most contribution lists are limited to the last 5 years.

Research description. CIHR: training expectations (up to 2 pages in English, 2.5 in French) and research project summary (1 page in English, 1.5 in French). NSERC: outline of proposed research (2 pages, natural sciences and engineering, plain language) with optional 5-page bibliography. SSHRC: research proposal (2 pages, 12 pt Times New Roman) and bibliography (up to 5 pages).

Contributions and experience. NSERC: contributions and statements (2 pages); SSHRC: research contributions and relevant experience (2 pages combined); CIHR: list of publications of up to 2 pages, with your role and percent contribution for multi-authored work. Optional 1-page special circumstances statement describing leaves, caregiving, illness, pandemic impact or similar.

Official, up-to-date transcripts for all undergraduate and graduate studies, completed or ongoing, with the legend for each, as one PDF. Official means issued by the registrar. CIHR also requires the CGRS D Timeline for Doctoral Studies form; SSHRC requires a certified English or French translation for other languages and a 1-page registrar letter if you studied part-time or had an approved interruption. Unofficial transcripts are accepted for NSERC review but your institution sets its own rule.

Two references (two sponsor assessments at CIHR, two letters of appraisal of one page each at SSHRC, two reference letters at NSERC), submitted online by the referees before the deadline. The application cannot be submitted until both are in. Choose people who can judge your research potential; you cannot explain your choice in the application.

Proof of citizenship status (CIHR, one page). Label it as Canadian Citizen, Permanent Resident, Protected Person or International Confirmation. International applicants may use a passport, birth certificate or a study or work permit valid on the submission date.

CIHR forms: CGRS D Confirmation of Scientific Area (1 page, signed by the primary supervisor), signature pages signed by supervisors, optional Indigenous Attestation Form, and optional Self-Declaration of No Institutional Affiliation with a Quota for direct applicants. Files must be unprotected PDFs under 30 MB at CIHR; NSERC filenames must be under 15 characters; SSHRC PDFs must be under 500 KB.
Certified translation of any supporting document that is not in English or French.
requirements.conditional_rule: If a document is in another language

application_steps.title: Confirm eligibility and choose the agency and channel
application_steps.detail: Check the 36-month study limit and that you are registered in a doctoral programme at an eligible Canadian institution (for international applicants). Pick the agency (CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC) closest to your research. Apply through your institution if it has a quota with that agency; otherwise apply directly to the agency. A wrong channel means rejection.

application_steps.title: Set up accounts, Common CV and referees
application_steps.detail: Register in the agency's online system, complete your Common CV, and name your two referees early; the application cannot be submitted until both reference assessments are in. At CIHR you also identify a primary supervisor who signs the scientific area form.

application_steps.title: Write the proposal, statements and upload transcripts
application_steps.detail: Prepare the research proposal or training expectations, contributions statement, transcripts and the other attachments in the agency's format and page limits. Documents over the limit may be removed without notice. After you submit, nothing can be changed except contact details.

application_steps.title: Meet the institution's deadline, then the agency's
application_steps.detail: Institutional deadlines are often much earlier than the agency's. Direct applicants submit by 8:00 pm Eastern on 17 October, or the next business day if that is a weekend (19 October 2026 in the SSHRC October 2026 competition; CIHR also gives 19 October, without a year on the page). Institutions forwarding quota applications had later cut-offs on the pages I read (CIHR 23 November, SSHRC 7 December). Late applications are not accepted.

application_steps.title: Institutional review within quota
application_steps.detail: If you apply through your institution, its graduate studies office checks eligibility and transcripts, ranks applications on the agency's selection criteria and forwards only those within its quota. CIHR says institutions tell applicants their internal outcome by 15 December.

application_steps.title: Agency committee review
application_steps.detail: Discipline-based review committees assess each application. Two criteria are weighted equally: research potential (50%: quality of the proposal, ability to carry it out, contributions, ethics, originality, communication) and relevant experience and achievements (50%: training, scholarships and awards, academic record, professional, academic and community activities). Committees consider special circumstances. Agencies may also award extra funding for priority research areas.

application_steps.title: Results
application_steps.detail: Results are sent by 30 April. Names and basic award information of accepted awardees are published on the agency website. SSHRC says an acknowledgement email with an application number arrives four to six weeks after the deadline.

application_steps.title: Accept the award and send the start paperwork
application_steps.detail: Successful applicants have 15 business days from the date on the funding decision letter to accept or decline. Before payment starts, the awardee emails one package with the signed Response to an Offer of Award, the Confirmation of Commencement (signed with the institution's scholarship liaison officer) and Proof of Registration. Awards can start only on 1 May, 1 September or 1 January and must match the programme start.

application_steps.title: Hold the award under tri-agency rules
application_steps.detail: You must stay eligible and make satisfactory progress for the full award, keep studies and research going (full time unless a part-time arrangement is approved), tell the agency right away if studies stop, and not hold another doctoral award from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC. Most programmes ask for annual progress reports. Interruptions and changes of institution, supervisor or topic need approval; unpaid and paid leaves extend the end date.

not_stated: Any English or French language test requirement (applications may be written in either language; no test or score stated)
Age limit or work experience requirement
Tuition fees, health cover, or travel being covered or not covered by the award (the pages describe only the CAD 40,000 a year)
Number of awards in total and per institution (quotas are named but numbers are not given on the pages read)

The exact deadline year for the 2027 cycle: the NSERC page gives 17 October with no year; the SSHRC page I read is for the October 2026 competition and the CIHR admin page gives a different date for institutions
A full application document checklist for NSERC and SSHRC in one place (read from their own instruction pages; CIHR's list is the most detailed)
fetch_problems: None blocked. The main NSERC page lists CIHR and SSHRC resources by name only; the NSERC page also shows a table of past recipients that did not come through.
notes: Dates differ by page: NSERC and CIHR give a direct-to-agency deadline of 17 and 19 October respectively (SSHRC's October 2026 page says 17 October fell on a weekend so the deadline moved to 19 October); CIHR's page for administrators gives 23 November as the date institutions must forward applications and 15 December for internal outcomes, while SSHRC gives 7 December for institution forwarding. Editors should check the agency page for the 2027 competition.

Stored data said CGRS D 'replaces the Vanier CGS'. The pages I read say the award is part of the Canada Research Training Awards Suite and that holders of any CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC doctoral award, including Vanier, are ineligible; I did not find the wording that it replaces Vanier on the pages read and did not repeat it.
Stored data was right that international students must already be registered in a Canadian doctoral programme; this is confirmed by NSERC and CIHR.
